properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's Model Development Kits 'implement DocGen language for dynamic, model-based document generation using view and viewpoint concepts'. Document generation is not a side feature there; it is half the value proposition, and the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere' is largely a claim about documents — write the model once, and every specification, review pack and report derives from it rather than drifting from it. WHERE reflow2 STANDS, and the gap is narrower than it first looks: reflow2 already has the same underlying idea. `docs/viewpoints.md` is DoDAF-informed, `dec:views-are-projections` states that a view is a pure projection of the graph and that renderer fill-ins are DEFECTS, and `tools/render_views.py` projects six viewpoints and CONFESSES anything a view needs that the graph cannot supply — with every confession counted as a finding (BL-40). That confession discipline is arguably stronger than DocGen's, because it makes the gaps in a document visible instead of filling them. THE HONEST DIFFERENCE IS PRODUCT, NOT CONCEPT: `render_views.py` is a probe in the tools directory, run by developers of reflow2. DocGen is something an engineering organisation hands to its systems engineers to produce the artefacts a programme is contractually required to deliver. reflow2 has never claimed the second, and `req:no-se-knowledge` ('the user never needs systems engineering') suggests it may not want to. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a document generator is a large surface with a long tail — templates, formats, numbering, review states — and every hour of it is an hour not spent on the coherence loop, which is the thing nobody else is building. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether the projections reflow2 already computes are close enough to what a real programme must deliver that the remaining distance is rendering rather than modelling.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2's viewpoints become a document product, the way DocGen is for OpenMBEE?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, ahead of a deep review against a clone of OpenMBEE's repository. The strength claim is deliberately hedged: reflow2 holds the concept (views as projections, confessions as findings) and OpenMBEE holds the product. Which of those is 'stronger' depends entirely on whether the user is a programme owing deliverables or a builder owing a coherent design, and reflow2 has so far chosen the second. Anthony's own position sits across both, which is why this is worth asking rather than assuming.
